about: DEFAULT OFF (Dom): `on` false hides the whole market (no merchant, chip, sheet, events or body fetch) unless the address carries ?<query>=<value>, i.e. ?market=1; `on` true shows it for everyone. The Flesh Market (Dom 2026-10-28: a shady merchant who trades harvested body parts, rare weapons and monster trophies, three items a day; docs/flesh-market.md). Local single-player economy in the data/progression.json save (the optional `market` field), paid in the BANKED coins of data/corpse-run.json (carried coins are at risk by design and are never spent or earned here). `merchant`: where he stands, as metres from the camp (the hero's start mark) in the zone frame, so he is in the safe yard; `body`/`kind` are the spawn ref the scene draws him from (a body already in src/assets, a stand-in until OpenTrident's mh-crowd-b1-02 lands: change these two rows only); `openMetres`: the Trade chip shows within this distance and `closeMetres`: the sheet closes beyond it; `loadMetres`: his body is fetched only within this distance of the hero (first-visit weight). `salt` + the UTC date seed the daily stock (src/market.ts stockFor): the same three items for everyone all day, whatever the player owns or does, so a reload or a sale cannot reroll it. `stock.slots`: the class of each of the three: `part` (a cut part of any boss, a rarity drawn by `weights`) or `any` (a part, or a weapon with `weights.weapon` against the three part weights). `price.base`: a part's value by rarity id (data/parts.json); he SELLS at base x `buyX` (rounded up) and BUYS at base x `sellX` (rounded down), validated so a sale never beats the rebuy of the same thing; `weapon`: a weapon's value by id (the pool is exactly these ids: a src/fight/weapon-defs.json row the hero can draw); `trophy`: a trophy's value by star tier (data/stars.json), bought from the player only. `caps`: no price above `buyMax`; at most `sellPerDay` coins of sales per UTC day; one purchase per stock item. `lines`: the merchant's words by event, picked by (date, trade count), never by a random call. `events`: the names emitted on the feel bus for the commentator. `ui`: the chip and the bottom sheet. Checked by src/market.ts validateMarket and src/sim/validate.js.

limits.about: Legal ranges the validator holds this file to, and the few engine numbers the market code reads: nothing here is tuning the player feels.
